title: Random forest predicts oxygen evolution activity and guides a new hydroxide catalyst
summary: A random forest model fitted composition, morphology, phase, electrolyte pH, electrode type and overpotential for transition metal hydroxide OER catalysts and predicted new experiments with a mean relative error of 4.74%. A designed Ni0.77Fe0.13La0.1 hydroxide was synthesised and showed an overpotential of 226 mV at 10 mA/cm2. The abstract does not state the training-set size or compare with other catalysts.
ai_technology: Random forest regression over hydroxide composition and condition descriptors
organization: University of Science and Technology Beijing

evidence.tested: Synthesis and electrochemical testing of the designed catalyst; model error 4.74% on new experiments.
evidence.unknown: Training data size and benchmark comparison not stated in the abstract; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A random forest predicted OER overpotential across doping space and was used to select the new composition.
